headline: Russia demands NATO withdraw forces to 1997 borders in Ukraine talks
summary: Russian negotiators in Abu Dhabi presented a document demanding NATO pull troops and bases back to 1997 borders and halt Western arms to Ukraine, The New York Times reported. Polish, Bulgarian, and Estonian leaders rejected the terms, which would end Baltic air policing and halt eastern deployments.
why_it_matters: Moscow's sweeping condition fuels fears along NATO's eastern flank that bilateral negotiations between Washington and Moscow could compromise collective European defense guarantees.
source_search: Russia demands NATO withdraw forces to 1997 borders in Ukraine talks DW

headline: Centre weighs PANI undersea cable project linking eight Andaman islands
summary: Union Telecommunications Secretary Amit Agrawal and Andaman Lieutenant Governor Dinesh Sharma reviewed plans on Saturday for the PANI submarine optical fibre network. Originating in Puri, Odisha, the cable would connect eight remote islands and provide an alternative backup route to the existing Chennai-Andaman network during service disruptions.
why_it_matters: Redundant submarine cabling alongside planned 4G expansion to 87 uncovered villages will improve emergency communications and bring reliable digital access to isolated island communities.
source_search: Centre weighs PANI undersea cable project linking eight Andaman islands The Hindu

headline: Mexican special forces capture FBI Most Wanted cartel boss El Chapo Isidro
summary: Mexican special forces backed by US intelligence captured FBI Most Wanted fugitive Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, alias El Chapo Isidro, in Guasave, Sinaloa on Friday night. Four soldiers and seven attackers died in gunbattles that forced civilians to flee a baseball game and triggered overnight roadblocks.
why_it_matters: Arresting a leader of the Beltrán Leyva and Sinaloa-allied trafficking network with a $5 million bounty disrupts major fentanyl and cocaine flows into the United States.
source_search: Mexican special forces capture FBI Most Wanted cartel boss El Chapo Isidro The Guardian

headline: India’s October energy import bill jumps 60% as Brent prices nearly double
summary: India’s net oil and gas import bill jumped 60% year-on-year to $16 billion in October as Brent crude averaged $124.77 a barrel, oil ministry data showed. Active domestic cooking-gas customers declined to 32.6 crore by November 1, while overall LPG usage fell 12.3% and diesel demand rose 12%.
why_it_matters: With imports meeting nearly 89% of India's crude demand, sustained high oil prices inflate the $97.7 billion fiscal-year energy bill and curb household cooking-gas usage.
source_search: India’s October energy import bill jumps 60% as Brent prices nearly double Hindu BusinessLine

headline: Maharashtra Rabi sowing plunges to 17% of normal, trailing 1972 drought
summary: Maharashtra farmers sowed just 10.02 lakh hectares of Rabi crops by November 16, representing 17% of the normal 57.8 lakh hectares. Sowing lags far behind the 47.2 lakh hectares recorded during the 1972 drought. With 74% of subdistricts under drought, growers are favouring cereals and pulses.
why_it_matters: Severe winter crop losses in a major agricultural state alongside persisting El Niño conditions threaten rural farm incomes and could tighten Indian foodgrain and oilseed supplies.
source_search: Maharashtra Rabi sowing plunges to 17% of normal, trailing 1972 drought Scroll.in

headline: Candy factory fire near Jakarta leaves three dead and 36 missing
summary: A fire tore through the PT Fonusa Agung Mulia candy factory in Indonesia's Banten province on Saturday, killing three people and leaving 36 workers unaccounted for. Firefighters battled flames for over 12 hours at the three-story Milkita plant, while rescue crews pulled 15 survivors from the blaze.
why_it_matters: Another deadly manufacturing blaze in Indonesia renews scrutiny over workplace safety standards and emergency preparedness across the country's industrial facilities.
source_search: Candy factory fire near Jakarta leaves three dead and 36 missing The Hindu

headline: Signal blocks mobile screenshots to counter OS-level AI screen scanning
summary: Messaging app Signal announced on Friday it is restricting mobile screenshots across Android and iOS to counter operating-system AI agents that scan user screens. President Meredith Whittaker warned that Windows, Android, and Apple systems risk exposing sensitive conversations to local databases or remote servers outside Signal's control.
why_it_matters: Built-in AI assistants scanning screens undermine Signal's privacy guarantees for every chat participant, and the screenshot block still leaves other sneaky data-access risks unresolved.
source_search: Signal blocks mobile screenshots to counter OS-level AI screen scanning TechCrunch

headline: India shifts green clearance for mid-sized non-coal mines to states
summary: The Union Environment Ministry notified an amendment on November 18 allowing state bodies to appraise non-coal mining projects up to 500 hectares for environmental clearance, doubling the previous 250-hectare limit. State authorities already evaluate coal mines up to that size, aligning both regimes under the revised 2006 notification.
why_it_matters: Decentralising clearances to state panels sharing identical expert criteria as central committees could speed up approvals for non-coal mining projects across India.
source_search: India shifts green clearance for mid-sized non-coal mines to states Hindu BusinessLine

headline: Wembanyama hits 50 points, five blocks as Spurs rout Pelicans
summary: San Antonio Spurs star Victor Wembanyama scored 50 points as his side beat the New Orleans Pelicans 114-91. The France international became the first NBA player to record 50 points, five blocks, and five threes since 1979-80. The Spurs now lead their division with 14 wins.
why_it_matters: After reaching the NBA Finals last season, San Antonio's fast start establishes Wembanyama's squad as genuine championship contenders in the Western Conference.
source_search: Wembanyama hits 50 points, five blocks as Spurs rout Pelicans BBC Sport

headline: Media body challenges Delhi Police over journalist detentions at Supreme Court
summary: The Network of Women in Media, India told the Supreme Court that Delhi Police cannot justify restraining journalists at October protests as mere crowd control. Filing a rejoinder on Saturday, the group argued lawful newsgathering covers freelance and digital reporters, while demanding an independent inquiry into closed harassment complaints.
why_it_matters: The court's ruling will clarify whether unaccredited freelance and digital journalists enjoy constitutional protection against police sweeps during public demonstrations in India.
source_search: Media body challenges Delhi Police over journalist detentions at Supreme Court Scroll.in

headline: Overturned funeral boat kills at least 24 in southern Nigeria
summary: An overcrowded passenger boat carrying hundreds of funeral mourners capsized on Friday in southern Nigeria's Bayelsa State after a mechanical failure, killing at least 24 people. Emergency officials said 24 survivors were rescued by Saturday as divers continued searching river waters while police detained the vessel's manager.
why_it_matters: Repeated fatal river accidents in Nigeria point to chronic overloading, poor vessel maintenance, and weak safety enforcement along busy inland waterways.
source_search: Overturned funeral boat kills at least 24 in southern Nigeria Al Jazeera

headline: Google pledges $5 million to IIT Kharagpur for applied AI research
summary: Google pledged $5 million to IIT Kharagpur during its platinum jubilee celebrations on November 21 to expand artificial intelligence research and campus infrastructure. Facilitated by alumnus and Google CEO Sundar Pichai, the grant targets Indic languages, agriculture, materials science, and educational technology alongside a $5-million alumnus data endowment.
why_it_matters: Funding applied research in local languages and agriculture boosts India's domestic AI talent pipeline and builds dedicated campus computing frameworks for students and faculty.
source_search: Google pledges $5 million to IIT Kharagpur for applied AI research Hindu BusinessLine

headline: South Korea education minister resigns over AI-assisted exam cheating scandal
summary: South Korean Education Minister Choi Kyo-jin resigned on Sunday after an AI-assisted cheating scandal ahead of Thursday's crucial Suneung college entrance exam. President Lee Jae Myung accepted the resignation after Choi drew backlash for doubting his ability to catch cheaters, while officials detected 111 electronic device violations.
why_it_matters: Public fury over miniature-camera cheating shows how rapidly AI tools are straining high-stakes national examination systems that govern university admissions and career prospects.
source_search: South Korea education minister resigns over AI-assisted exam cheating scandal The Hindu

headline: Maruti Suzuki raises select vehicle prices amid sustained cost pressures
summary: Maruti Suzuki India raised prices across select models by a volume-weighted average of 0.31% on Sunday, citing sustained cost pressures. The adjustment follows three hikes totalling over 1% earlier in FY27 after higher input costs from the West Asia conflict weighed on second-quarter net profit.
why_it_matters: Frequent calibrated price increases show India's largest carmaker protecting operating margins against geopolitical supply costs while trying not to dampen strong domestic demand.
source_search: Maruti Suzuki raises select vehicle prices amid sustained cost pressures The Hindu

headline: Paredes collapses from heat after Boca Juniors win Copa Sudamericana title
summary: Argentina midfielder Leandro Paredes collapsed during an interview after Boca Juniors beat Atletico Mineiro by two goals to win the Copa Sudamericana in Colombia. Overcoming 32C heat and 80% humidity, the midfielder recovered to celebrate. The victory ended an 18-year drought and set a continental trophy record.
why_it_matters: Extreme tropical conditions in Barranquilla raise player welfare concerns in South American finals, even as Boca Juniors reclaimed continental supremacy over rivals Independiente.
source_search: Paredes collapses from heat after Boca Juniors win Copa Sudamericana title BBC Sport

headline: Scotland orders NHS Grampian review after whistleblower reveals 19 avoidable deaths
summary: Scottish Health Secretary Angela Constance ordered an urgent independent review into hepatobiliary surgery at NHS Grampian after whistleblower Dr Mohammed Habib leaked a 2022 report. The document found 19 of 31 deaths in liver and pancreatic procedures were avoidable. Constance will detail the inquiry timetable in Holyrood on Tuesday.
why_it_matters: Because Habib raised warnings four times earlier without action, the inquiry will test how Scottish health boards and ministers handle patient safety alerts and clinical accountability.
source_search: Scotland orders NHS Grampian review after whistleblower reveals 19 avoidable deaths BBC

headline: Over 100 children hospitalised after village fair meal in Madhya Pradesh
summary: Suspected food poisoning sent 118 children and 12 adults to hospitals after eating chowmein at a village fair in Madhya Pradesh's Balaghat district on Saturday evening. Officials confirmed on Sunday that 73 children were discharged after primary care while 45 children and 12 adults remain stable.
why_it_matters: Mass food-poisoning incidents at rural gatherings expose gaps in local street-food hygiene monitoring and strain district community health centres.
source_search: Over 100 children hospitalised after village fair meal in Madhya Pradesh The Hindu

headline: US immigration agents arrest two on Seattle airport jet bridge
summary: Masked US immigration agents arrested two people on a Seattle-Tacoma airport jet bridge during Saturday morning boarding for Los Angeles, delaying the Alaska Airlines flight by three hours. Washington Governor Bob Ferguson condemned the unannounced operation and urged airlines to ask federal agents to leave airports.
why_it_matters: Unannounced federal enforcement inside airport boarding zones escalates tensions between Democratic state leaders, commercial carriers, and federal immigration authorities during peak travel.
source_search: US immigration agents arrest two on Seattle airport jet bridge DW

headline: UN Geneva talks stall on binding rules for autonomous ‘killer robots’
summary: United Nations diplomats meeting in Geneva failed to reach binding rules on autonomous weapons, agreeing instead to give countries two years to propose potential regulations. Despite urgent calls from the International Committee of the Red Cross, Russia, Israel, and the United States obstructed tougher, legally enforceable restrictions.
why_it_matters: With semi-autonomous drones already causing civilian deaths in Ukraine, Gaza, and Sudan, leaving future guidelines optional risks years of unregulated deployment in active conflicts.
source_search: UN Geneva talks stall on binding rules for autonomous ‘killer robots’ The Verge

headline: BJP Rajya Sabha MP Ramrao Wadkute dies in Delhi at 72
summary: BJP Rajya Sabha MP Ramrao Sakharam Wadkute died of a cardiac arrest at AIIMS in New Delhi late Saturday night at age 72. Elected to the Upper House from Maharashtra's Marathwada region in April, the veteran cooperative and Dhangar community leader had been admitted for a cough.
why_it_matters: His death leaves a Maharashtra Rajya Sabha vacancy and deprives the ruling BJP of an influential grassroots organiser from the Marathwada region.
source_search: BJP Rajya Sabha MP Ramrao Wadkute dies in Delhi at 72 The Hindu

headline: Officers panel to review GST law changes protecting genuine buyers
summary: A 23-member Standing Committee of Officers will examine five draft amendments to the Central GST Act to protect genuine businesses from losing input tax credit over supplier defaults. The panel has three months to submit recommendations to the GST Council, targeting implementation in financial year 2027-28.
why_it_matters: Separating innocent recipients from upstream supplier defaults while inserting an explicit fraud-denial rule would stop compliant businesses from paying for another party's tax violation.
source_search: Officers panel to review GST law changes protecting genuine buyers Hindu BusinessLine

headline: Conway fifty keeps New Zealand fighting after India declare at 720
summary: Devon Conway hit an unbeaten half-century to guide New Zealand to 119 for two at stumps on day four of the first Test in Wellington, trailing India by 233 runs. Earlier, Rishabh Pant smashed 128 off 153 balls before India declared at a commanding 720 for nine.
why_it_matters: With eight wickets remaining on a flat Basin Reserve pitch, New Zealand must bat through the final day to salvage a draw against India's pace attack.
source_search: Conway fifty keeps New Zealand fighting after India declare at 720 The Hindu

headline: Karla Sofia Gascon links Oscar backlash to anti-trans bias at IFFI Goa
summary: Spanish actor Karla Sofia Gascon said at the International Film Festival of India in Goa that her Oscar campaign controversy stemmed from people opposing a transgender winner. Premiering her Western film Trinidad at IFFI, the Emilia Pérez star criticised political pressures in awards races and regression in transgender rights.
why_it_matters: Her remarks show how culture-war politics increasingly shape major film awards campaigns, even as breakthrough Oscar recognition opens international casting doors for underrepresented actors.
source_search: Karla Sofia Gascon links Oscar backlash to anti-trans bias at IFFI Goa Variety

headline: Rogue casinos hijack UK gambling researchers' identities to lure online bettors
summary: Nearly 30 casino websites hijacked the names and photos of at least six UK gambling researchers, including Glasgow academic Heather Wardle. Fake biographies falsely claim they endorse unlicensed operators outside Britain's GamStop protection scheme. Affiliates also bought unrelated domains to lure unsuspecting visitors into offshore betting.
why_it_matters: Co-opting trusted scholars and non-gambling websites lets illicit operators bypass UK consumer safeguards and steer vulnerable people toward unregulated, high-risk betting platforms.
source_search: Rogue casinos hijack UK gambling researchers' identities to lure online bettors The Guardian

headline: NHS Wales pauses national midwife recruitment drive, leaving graduates without jobs
summary: Health Education and Improvement Wales cancelled its spring 2027 national midwife recruitment round, warning upcoming graduates of scarce vacancies. Last year, 66 newly qualified midwives found no roles despite NHS Wales funding their tuition. Budget limits now block Band 5 hires even as maternity staff report heavy pressure.
why_it_matters: Training midwives with public tuition grants while failing to fund entry-level hospital roles wastes taxpayer money and strains already stretched Welsh maternity wards.
source_search: NHS Wales pauses national midwife recruitment drive, leaving graduates without jobs BBC
